TCP vs UDP: When to Use Which: storyboard

Episode 5 · voice Liam · 9 scenes · 82.8s (measured timing) · one still per beat, 8 frames after it fires

hook hook Hook · 0.0s–7.9s

Headline: Careful or fast?

“Netflix runs on TCP, but your online game runs on UDP. Why would anything choose the sloppy one?”

branding sting 7.9s–9.4s

Bite wipe → logos → cut. No voiceover, just the chomp.

idea idea Diorama · 9.4s–18.9s

Headline: Courier or postcard

“Both carry data between machines. TCP is a courier who waits for your signature. UDP drops postcards in the mailbox and walks away.”

breakdown handshake Sequence · 18.9s–29.0s

Headline: Handshake first

“TCP starts with a handshake. The client says hello, the server says hello back, then okay. Only then does data move.”

breakdown resend Sequence · 29.0s–37.6s

No headline

“Then every chunk gets a receipt. If one goes missing, it's sent again. Nothing is lost, and it all arrives in order.”

breakdown udp Sequence · 37.6s–45.1s

Headline: Fire and forget

“UDP skips all that. No handshake, no receipts, no resends. A lost packet is just gone.”

breakdown speed Split · 45.1s–53.3s

Headline: Checking costs time

“Checking costs time. TCP double-checks, so it's slower. UDP just sends, so it wins the race.”

breakdown trade Matrix · 53.3s–64.5s

No headline

“The trade: TCP keeps data complete and in order, great for downloads. UDP stays quick and light, great for games. Pick what you can live without.”

breakdown rule Decision · 64.5s–76.9s

Headline: Is late useless?

“Ask one question: is late data useless? In a game, yes, so UDP. A movie can buffer, so Netflix waits for TCP.”

gist gist GistCard · 76.9s–82.8s

No headline

“That's the gist: TCP never loses data, UDP never waits. Follow for more.”
